thread.title: Wolfe Research Initiates Coverage on Apple (AAPL)

author: Christopher Mengel
title: Wolfe Research Initiates Coverage on Apple (AAPL)
text:
Posted by Christopher Mengel on Jan 6th, 2019 // No Comments
Stock analysts at Wolfe Research started coverage on shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) in a research note issued to investors on Tuesday, December 11th, The Fly reports. The firm set a “market perform” rating on the iPhone maker’s stock.
AAPL has been the topic of a number of other reports. Wedbush raised shares of Apple to an “outperform” rating and dropped their price objective for the company from $310.00 to $275.00 in a research report on Wednesday, November 28th. They noted that the move was a valuation call. New Street Research cut shares of Apple from a “neutral” rating to a “sell” rating in a report on Monday, August 20th. Morgan Stanley increased their price target on shares of Apple from $226.00 to $253.00 and gave the stock an “overweight” rating in a research note on Thursday, November 8th. JPMorgan Chase & Co. set a $272.00 price target on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Monday, October 29th. Finally, UBS Group decreased their price target on shares of Apple from to and set a “buy” rating for the company in a research note on Monday, November 12th. Three investment analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twenty-six have assigned a hold rating and twenty-one have given a buy rating to the company. Apple currently has an average rating of “Hold” and a consensus price target of $195.64. Get Apple alerts:
Shares of NASDAQ AAPL traded up $6.07 during trading on Tuesday, hitting $148.26. The company had a trading volume of 57,415,139 shares, compared to its average volume of 61,934,055. The firm has a market cap of $775.31 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 12.45, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.21 and a beta of 1.23. Apple has a fifty-two week low of $142.00 and a fifty-two week high of $233.47. The company has a quick ratio of 1.09, a current ratio of 1.12 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its earnings results on Thursday, November 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.91 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $2.78 by $0.13. The company had revenue of $62.90 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $61.55 billion. Apple had a net margin of 22.41% and a return on equity of 48.68%. Apple’s revenue was up 19.6% on a year-over-year basis. During the same period in the previous year, the business posted $2.07 EPS. Equities research analysts anticipate that Apple will post 13.18 EPS for the current fiscal year.
In other news, insider Chris Kondo sold 3,408 shares of Apple stock in a transaction that occurred on Monday, November 19th. The shares were sold at an average price of $190.00, for a total transaction of $647,520.00. Following the sale, the insider now owns 8,940 shares in the company, valued at $1,698,600. The transaction was disclosed in a legal filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is available at the SEC website . Company insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock.

Trillium Asset Management LLC now owns 129,850 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $21,786,000 after purchasing an additional 15,657 shares during the period. Finally, Canandaigua National Bank & Trust Co. boosted its holdings in Apple by 0.5% in the first quarter. Canandaigua National Bank & Trust Co. now owns 51,711 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $8,676,000 after purchasing an additional 280 shares during the period. Apple Company Profile
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers. It also sells various related software, services, accessories, and third-party digital content and applications. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and Mac, a line of desktop and portable personal computers, as well as iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS operating systems.
